curriculum.title: Wisdom, Poetry, and Reading by Genre

core.big_idea: Genre shapes meaning: poems, proverbs, and wisdom arguments must not be read as flat propositions.

passages.reading_note: Read the central passage with attention to context and age-appropriate scope.
Use only where it directly clarifies the central lesson.
Use only where it directly clarifies the central lesson.

core.metanarrative_position: Wisdom and poetry: genre controls how claims, images, tensions, and conclusions are read.

claims.statement: Psalm 73 presents a poetic movement from envy and confusion toward renewed perspective in worship.
Proverbs 26:4-5 places apparently opposite instructions side by side, showing that proverbs require situational wisdom.
Ecclesiastes develops an extended argument and ends with a concluding call to fear God and keep His commandments.
Reading each text according to genre is necessary to avoid flattening poetry, proverbs, and wisdom reflection into identical kinds of propositions.
claims.prohibited_overstatement: Do not state this claim more strongly than the evidence and classification allow.

core.interpretation_skill: Identify genre and context, separate direct observation from synthesis or inference, and connect the passage to the whole-Bible story without forced symbolism.

learning.foundation_objective: Explain in age-appropriate language that genre shapes meaning: poems, proverbs, and wisdom arguments must not be read as flat propositions.
learning.extension_objective: Locate the lesson in the whole-Bible story and distinguish direct textual claims from later synthesis or application.
know: The central passage is Psalm 73; Proverbs 26:4-5; Ecclesiastes 12:9-14.
Genre shapes meaning: poems, proverbs, and wisdom arguments must not be read as flat propositions.
The lesson belongs within the wider biblical storyline.
understand: Biblical meaning depends on context and genre.
Application should follow what the text supports rather than replace it.
practise: Use one observation question before giving an interpretation.
Compare a psalm and a proverb and ask how the form changes the way each should be applied.
become: A learner who reads Scripture carefully and responds with trust, wisdom, and love.
success_evidence: Student can retell or summarize the central passage.
Student can state the big idea without adding unsupported details.
Student can name one appropriate response.

zero_prep_card.objective: Explain in age-appropriate language that genre shapes meaning: poems, proverbs, and wisdom arguments must not be read as flat propositions.
zero_prep_card.opening: Ask: What do you notice first in this passage, before we explain what it means?
say: Psalm 73 presents a poetic movement from envy and confusion toward renewed perspective in worship.
Proverbs 26:4-5 places apparently opposite instructions side by side, showing that proverbs require situational wisdom.

We will separate what the passage says from what we infer or apply.

preparation.passage_context: Wisdom and poetry: genre controls how claims, images, tensions, and conclusions are read.
text_observations: Psalm 73 presents a poetic movement from envy and confusion toward renewed perspective in worship.
Proverbs 26:4-5 places apparently opposite instructions side by side, showing that proverbs require situational wisdom.
Ecclesiastes develops an extended argument and ends with a concluding call to fear God and keep His commandments.
Reading each text according to genre is necessary to avoid flattening poetry, proverbs, and wisdom reflection into identical kinds of propositions.
interpretation_notes: Start with the principal passage before moving to supporting texts.
Keep genre and original audience visible.
Label synthesis, historical context, and application rather than presenting them as quotations.
theological_guardrails: Do not use “genre” as a device for dismissing claims you dislike.
Do not treat every proverb as an unconditional promise.
Keep literary form and canonical context together.

likely_questions.question: Does genre mean a passage is less true?
likely_questions.purpose: No. Genre describes how a text communicates truth and therefore how it should be read.

likely_questions.question: Why do Proverbs 26:4 and 26:5 seem contradictory?
likely_questions.purpose: They place two situationally appropriate responses together, requiring wisdom about when each applies.

accessibility.plain_language_rule: Prefer short sentences, define unfamiliar biblical terms, and do not require independent reading beyond the segment.
neurodiversity_supports: Give instructions one step at a time.
Allow verbal, written, or pointing responses.
Preview transitions and allow a pass option.
sensory_notes: No activity requires loud sound, forced touch, or competitive speed.
non_reader_support: Teacher or parent may read aloud.
Use sequence cards, symbols, or oral responses.

do_not_ask: Do not require disclosure of private family circumstances.
Do not require public confession or religious decision.
Do not use physical touch without consent.
safeguarding.teacher_response: If a child discloses harm, danger, abuse, severe distress, or unmet basic needs, follow the congregation safeguarding process rather than trying to investigate in class.
